title: Heal admission reservoir leak and reinstate fairness for mixed-length flows
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A production defect in the batch admission reservoir algorithm allows long-context requests to slowly exhaust reservoir credits, causing repeated preemption of short, latency-sensitive requests and driving P99/P999 for short flows well beyond SLOs. This ticket consolidates customer escalations from Hosted and Dedicated customers, diagnoses the admission-credit leak, implements a conservative fix with a feature-flagged rollout, and validates through targeted canaries and synthetic mixes.

Background: Over the past 10 days we observed a correlated spike in short-request tail latency coinciding with higher long-context churn. The scheduler's admission reservoir is intended to amortize capacity between long and short sequences, but under fluctuating KV-cache handoffs and irregular dequeue timing, credits are not replenished predictably and are biased toward active long requests. Several enterprise customers (notably AcmePay and MedicaCloud) opened escalations when short interactive calls hit P99 > 2s.

Objective: Fix the reservoir bookkeeping leak, add defensive invariants, and restore proportional admission so small requests regain latency SLOs without sacrificing throughput for long-context batches. Provide a safe rollback and observability to detect regressions early.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy runtime-1.20 with admission reservoir enabled in a cluster with mixed tenant profiles (70% short seq <64, 30% long seq >2048).
2) Fire a steady stream of short requests (qps 120) while intermittently bursting long-context generation jobs (every 30s, 12 concurrent long flows).
3) Observe scheduler admission credits and dequeue logs; after ~5 minutes credits for short-class drop and starve; P99 for short requests increases from baseline ~120ms to >2s.
4) Collect /metrics and /debug/scheduler snapshots for timeline alignment and KV cache handoff events.
observed_behavior: Admission reservoir balance drifts monotonically toward long requests during mixed bursts.
Short-class batches experience preemption and are queued behind persistent long batches.
KV cache eviction churn often coincides with depletion windows, amplifying dequeue stalls.
Customer escalations cited interactive UX timeouts and retriable errors from SDK timeouts.
root_cause_analysis: A combination of two bugs: (A) credit-topup ran on a per-shard timer that could be delayed by GC/stop-the-world pauses causing skewed replenishment; (B) when a long batch preempted, its KV-handoff path didn't decrement its 'active reservation' flag on some code paths, leaving logical credits consumed without being released.
Race between admission top-up and preemptive dequeue allowed long flows to accumulate soft-credits across scheduling epochs.
Edge-case: dedicated tenant quotas with burst windows were using a different reservation counter causing cross-path inconsistency.
fix_summary: 1) Make top-up idempotent and anchored to an epoch counter instead of wall-clock timers; if top-up is delayed we perform bounded catch-up rather than a full refill to avoid sudden credit spikes.

2) Add robust release paths: ensure every code path that consumes a reservation (including error and cancellation paths) decrements the active_reservation counter using scoped RAII-style guard objects in C++ runtime and equivalent try/finally in Go components.
3) Align reservation counters across Dedicated and Hosted code paths by introducing a thin compatibility shim and tests to assert invariants across both flows.
4) Add invariant checks that emit trace events and metrics when reservoir skew exceeds 20% for >30s.
qa_checks: Unit tests for reservation guard and epoch top-up logic.
Deterministic scheduler simulation with mixed-length workload generator (small/large ratio sweep).
Load test: 30-minute mixed workload at production qps; measure P50/P95/P99 for short-class and long-class. Target: short-class P99 < 250ms under baseline mix.
Chaos test: inject small GC pauses and KV eviction events during load test to validate robustness.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Canary on internal dedicated cluster (1 node), 2 hours smoke + perf runs.
Stage 2: Canary tenant group (non-customer tenants with synthetic mixed workloads), 6 hours with SLO guardrails.
Stage 3: Select customer canaries (AcmePay staging and one Hosted trial), 24 hours monitoring and manual approval.
Stage 4: Gradual ramp to 30% of cluster fleet, then 100% if no regressions for 48h.
Rollback: flip FF off and revert admission shim tag; fallback path preserves pre-fix behavior.
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: scheduler_reservoir_skew_ratio > 0.2 for 5m triggers PagerDuty P1.
Dashboard: mixed-length fairness panel with short/long P95/P99, reservation credits over time, and KV eviction rate correlation plot.
metrics_after_fix: Canary observed short-class P99 reduced from 2.3s to 160ms under synthetic mixed load.
Overall throughput for long-class unchanged within 2% of baseline.
Reservoir skew metric stabilized below 0.05 in 95th percentile over 1h runs.

notes: Open questions: do we need a persistent reservation quota per-tenant to protect small tenants from long-tenant floods? Also evaluate if admission reservoir should be replaced by a token-bucket per-class model. Follow-up spike planned (ENG-81211) to evaluate token-bucket redesign.
